title: George Orwell's birth chart
metaDescription: George Orwell's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 2.5° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Mars and Saturn sit 0.1° from an exact trine — near enough that the tradition reads drive and structure as a single working part. A trine runs downhill — the talent that never announces itself because it never had to.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Cancer, but precisely: 2.5°, first decan, 0°–10°, under the Moon in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Mercury holds 11.0° Gemini, Venus holds 17.3° Leo, Mars holds 8.4° Libra — in the old shorthand, a mind at home in argument and pattern; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The tightest geometry in the chart puts Mars a third of the circle apart from Saturn, 0.1° off exact. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required. Behind it, Jupiter square Uranus at 0.5°, and the Sun conjunction Neptune at 0.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: Mercury, Mars, Saturn close a triangle of trines. The closed triangle is the scheme’s picture of flow — and its warning that flow, unspent, stays private. Uranus opposes Pluto while both square Jupiter. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has four entries for this chart. Mercury in Gemini at 11.0° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mars in Libra at 8.4° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Pisces at 22.7° is in domicile; Saturn in Aquarius at 8.3° is in domicile. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The honest balance sheet uses the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: air 4, water 3, fire 2 across the elements, and mutable 4, cardinal 3, fixed 2 across the modalities. Air runs on comparison and connection — the pattern noticed first, the feeling filed second. No settled placement falls in earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Gemini into Cancer during that day at the birthplace, travelling 15.2° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
